questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

A ______ souvenir will be released on the occasion of the World Meet.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**voluminous**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• '**Souvenir**' is a thing that is kept as a reminder of a person, place, or event. (यादगार)

 
 
• **Example**: The recording provides a **souvenir** of a great production.
 
 
 
• '**Voluminous**' means having or marked by great volume or bulk; large. (विशाल-काय)
 
 
• **Example**: A **voluminous** purple cloak.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, it is clearly mentioned that a large souvenir will be released on the occasion of the World Meet.
 
• Some **synonyms** of the word '**voluminous**' are **large, bulky, ample, abundant, massive**.
 
• Some **antonyms **of the word '**voluminous**' are** little, small, slight, tiny.**
 
• Therefore, the most appropriate option to be filled in the given blank is '**voluminous**'.
 
• Hence, **option 2** is the** correct answer.**

 

**The complete sentence is: **__*A **voluminous** souvenir will be released on the occasion of the World Meet.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**Let's learn about other given options:

 
• '**Considerable**' means notably large in size, amount, or extent. (पर्याप्त)

 
 
• **Example**: A position of **considerable** influence.
 
 
 
• '**Generous**' means showing a readiness to give more of something, as money or time, than is strictly necessary or expected. (उदार)
 
 
• **Example**: She was **generous** with her money.
 
 
 
• '**Bountiful**' means large in quantity. (भरपूर)
 
 
• **Example**: The ocean provided a **bountiful** supply of fresh food.

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into four parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.**

The Principal requested / the teacher’s / to monitor / and take care of the small children.

options.text: and take care of the small children

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"the teacher's".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence the **error** lies in** the part "the teacher's"**.
 
• We use an **apostrophe +"s" **to show that **one person/thing owns or is a member of something**.
 
 
• Example: The shop's customers.
 
 
 
• We use an apostrophe after the "s" (s') at the end of a **plural noun to show possession.**
 
• If a plural noun doesn't end in **"s,"** add an apostrophe + "s" to create the possessive form.
 
• We use** 's'** to** pluralize the regular nouns.**
 
 
• **Example**: I have one cat; you have two **cats**.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence there are many teachers who have to take care of the children.
 
• Therefore,** "the teacher's" **should be replaced with **"the teachers"**.
 
• Hence, **option 1** is the** correct answer.**

**The correct sentence is: **__*The Principal requested **the teachers** to monitor and take care of the small children.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Let's learn about some more rules of **possessives**:

 
 
• When something belongs to more than one person and we give a list of names, we put 's on the last name.
 
• **Examples**:
 
 
• **Sam's **and **Emma's** house. (**Incorrect)**
 
• **Sam **and** Emma's** house. (**Correct**)
 
 
 
• **Possessives** have no long form.
 
• **Examples**: 
 
 
• Here is** Jack** is room. (**Incorrect)**
 
• Here is** Jack's** room. (**Correct**)

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. This invention has helped us to heal wounds caused by bacteria.

B. Penicillin is one of the most useful drugs man has invented.

C. In the beginning, however, very few people knew of this discovery and its use.

D. Its use has saved the lives of hundreds of thousands of soldiers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**BADC**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• While carefully reading all the statements, it is clear that** sentence B** is the **introductory statement.**
 
• **Sentence B** will come in the **first place** because it is introducing us to the topic of '**penicillin**'.
 
• **Sentence A** will come in the **second place** because it is telling us how the invention of penicillin has helped us.
 
• It is telling us that it has helped us to heal wounds caused by bacteria.
 
• **Sentence D** will come in the **third place** because it is telling us that by healing wounds it has saved the lives of hundreds of thousands of soldiers.
 
• **Sentence C **will come in the **last place **because it is telling us that its discovery and use were known to very few people in the beginning.
 
• Therefore, the **correct sequence** is '**BADC**'.
 
• Hence, **option 4** is the** correct answer.**

 

**The correct sequence is:**__ *Penicillin is one of the most useful drugs man has invented. This invention has helped us to heal wounds caused by bacteria. Its use has saved the lives of hundreds of thousands of soldiers. In the beginning, however, very few people knew of this discovery and its use.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• '**Heal**' means (of a person or treatment) cause (a wound, injury, or person) to become sound or healthy again. (ठीक होना)

 
 
• **Example**: His concern is to **heal** sick people.
 
 
 
• '**Wound**' means an injury to living tissue caused by a cut, blow, or other impact, typically one in which the skin is cut or broken. (घाव)
 
 
• **Example**: A knife **wound**.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'too noisy'**.

__
 
• ‘**Much**’ is used when we are speaking about a **singular noun.**
 
• **“Too much” **means that there is an excess of something.
 
• “**Too**” is used to describe that the adjective or adverb being used is in an excessive or extreme state, while “**mu​ch**” describes the fact that this phrase describes the quantity of something.
 
• In the given sentence,** 'too noisy'** is most appropriate.
 
• Hence, **option 4** is the** correct answer.**

 

**The correct sentence is: **__*The place is** too noisy.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• We often use **too** before **much** and **many**.
 
• We can use **too** **much** before an **uncountable noun** and **too many **before a **plural noun**, or **without a noun** when the **noun** is obvious:
 
 
• **Example**: I bought **too much** food. We had to throw some of it away.

**Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.**

I wish I __have__ come an hour sooner.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**had**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **the past perfect tense.**
 
• The **past perfect** is used when two events happened in the past, with one past action having occurred even before the other past action.
 
• To form the** past perfect**, use **'had' **and the** 'past participle of a verb'** in one part of the sentence.
 
• We use the **past perfect (had + past participle)** to talk about time up to a certain point in the past.
 
 
• **Example**: She** had published** her first poem by the time she was eight.
 
 
 
• We use **wish + past form verb** when we want something now or in the future to be different.
 
 
• **Example**: I wish I **had** more money.
 
 
 
• We use** wish + past perfect verb** to show we regret something (we want something in the past to be different).
 
 
• **Example**: I wish I **had** listened to my mom and studied harder.
 
 
 
• Therefore, in the given sentence, '**have**' should be replaced with '**had**' because the speaker is regretting coming late and wish that he should have come an hour early.
 
• Hence, **option 3** is the **correct answer.**

 

**The correct sentence is:__* ****I wish I **had** come an hour sooner. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• We can use the past perfect to show the order of two past events. The past perfect shows the earlier action and the past simple shows the later action.
 
 
• **Example**: When the police arrived, the thief **had** escaped.
 
 
 
• Note that if there's only a single event, we don't use the past perfect, even if it happened a long time ago.
 
 
• **Example**: The Romans had spoken Latin. (Incorrect)
 
 

 The Romans spoke Latin. (Correct)
